hook: CJI in Hyderabad: AI detectors wrongly flag *3 in 5* non-native essays
hook_b: CJI in Hyderabad: AI detectors wrongly flag *3 in 5* non-native essays
tldr: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant told a Commonwealth legal education conference in Hyderabad that no student should be held guilty of misconduct on a machine's word alone.

beats.what: Opening the two-day CLEA conference, the CJI said banning AI tools would be neither practical nor wise, and colleges need clear rules on how students may use them.
beats.why: He cited a study finding widely used detectors wrongly marked more than three in five essays by non-native English speakers as machine-written.
beats.care: Students could see oral explanations and error-spotting in AI answers added to written tests, as he suggested.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: He asked CLEA to draft model guidelines on disclosing AI help in legal research for law schools and journals.

cards.q: Should colleges use AI detectors to judge student work?

qs: Do Hyderabad colleges tell students which AI detector they use and how it is checked?

facts.t: This is the *first* international edition of the CLEA conference, held in Hyderabad.

viz.verdict: Honest students risk being branded cheats, the CJI said
Rules for AI use, not a ban

steps.e: Add oral explanations and error-spotting in AI answers
Compulsory legal aid work before graduation

watch: Whether CLEA drafts model guidelines on disclosing AI use in legal research.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: 'No student should be held guilty on word of machine alone': CJI Surya Kant at legal education conference in Hyderabad

fact: AI detectors wrongly flagged *3 in 5* non-native English essays, CJI said in Hyderabad
twist: He also proposed making legal aid work compulsory for every law student before graduation.
